headline: PayPal G&S vs Friends & Family
description: Understand PayPal Goods & Services fees (3.49%+$0.49 US) versus Friends & Family $0 personal payments—protections, risks, and when each is appropriate.

acceptedAnswer.text: It can be $0 for eligible personal payments funded from PayPal balance or linked bank. Other funding sources can add fees. Confirm on PayPal’s official fees page—do not use F&F for commercial sales to chase $0.

mainEntity.name: How much is Goods & Services on $100?

acceptedAnswer.text: About $3.98 in fees (3.49% + $0.49), net about $96.02, using US list G&S as of 2026-10-15. Confirm in /tools/paypal-fee-calculator/.

mainEntity.name: Can I offer a discount for F&F?

acceptedAnswer.text: You should not steer commercial buyers to F&F to avoid fees. That practice risks policy issues and protection gaps. Offer discounts for other legitimate methods only if your processor and laws allow.

mainEntity.name: What if a client already sent F&F?

acceptedAnswer.text: Follow your written policy. Many freelancers pause work until funds are resent as G&S or refunded. Document communication. Do not treat accidental F&F as a loophole.

Protections depend on eligibility, category, and following PayPal’s requirements (tracking, proof of delivery, etc.). Read PayPal’s seller protection terms for your country—fees buy access to a commercial framework, not a guarantee in every dispute.
